newsitem.title: MEXICO: Election unlikely to sway rating on Mexico - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Election unlikely to sway rating on Mexico - S&P.

text.p: The outcome of Mexico's mid-term elections is unlikely to bring it a rating increase, Standard and Poor's analyst Lacey Gallagher said on Thursday.
"It is important to point out that the rating factors in an expected base case scenerio. We didn't learn much more on election day," Gallagher said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

Final data is not in yet, but preliminary results have shown the ruling the Institutional Revolutionary Part (PRI) has likely lost its outright majority in the lower house of Congress, the Chamber of Deputies.

The conservative National Action Party (PAN) and the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) both made big gains in Congress, while PRD candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas won the job as Mexico City's first elected mayor since the 1920s.
The PAN also increased the number of state governor posts it holds.
Gallagher said the elections were relatively clean and fair, and that the influence and power of the opposition grew as expected with the vote on July 6.
"Those things were as expected and therefore would not change our ratings at this moment," said Gallagher.
She said important challenges remained, including the delicate process of multi-party negotiations to pass legislation, and seeing what effect this may have on party unity.
She also pointed to the possibility of sluggish consumption that could cause even weaker support for the government and raise questions about how the PRI would react.
On the other hand, stronger consumption could heighten a balance of payments risk, she said.
"We need to wait and see a bit how these very important challenges, these unknowns, as opposed to the expected results of the election, play out," she said.
Standard & Poor's has a double B rating with a stable outlook on Mexico's long-term foreign currency obligations.
